item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Did this seem to anyone else like it was written by someone who speaks English as their second language? There was just some really odd sentence construction here and there, like when the hallway was "applied with SCP-622." Did you mean the hallway was "coated with SCP-622" or that "SCP-622 was applied" to the hallway? Also, the shelf-life of something is how long it can sit on the shelf, unused, before it loses efficacy, not how long it takes to stop working after you've used it. I really thought that first test was going to involve a super old can of the stuff.

And if the researchers thought the facility's ventilation system was messing with their data, why didn't they isolate the control hallways as well as the test hallway?

Aside from the word choice issues, I would really like to see this rewritten, as I think it has the potential to be something more than just an anomalously powerful desiccant. Desert in a Can! How can it not be more?

This doesn't do much for me. It just sort of repeats the same point, but more so each time until it's really strangely over-the-top.

Also, not to press on a common complaint, but:

Special Containment Procedures: All cans and containers of SCP-622 are to be immediately transferred to Site ██.

I don't see the point here. What the duck is a containment team supposed to do if they come across a box of cans, but they don't know where to send them because the location was redacted?

I would be interested in seeing a cleaned up or rewritten version of this, however, because with some good writing and fresh ideas this has the potential to be quite good.
